title: Model quantization playbook and acceptance criteria for catalog defaults
creator: Mei Chen
description:
Goal: Establish a reproducible playbook and numeric acceptance criteria for assigning per-model quantization defaults in the model catalog. Outputs: (1) a set of recommended profiles (FP8/INT8/mixed), (2) a deterministic calibration workflow and CI gating rules, (3) a guardrail matrix and automatic fallback chain, and (4) dashboards/alerts for post-rollout monitoring.

Background: We need consistent defaults in the catalog so customers get predictable latency/cost improvements with bounded quality risk. Existing patchwork of heuristics causes surprising regressions during rollouts. This ticket scopes the end-to-end policy and the verification steps required for safe defaults.

Scope and non-goals:
- In scope: per-model default profile selection (prod catalog), calibration dataset spec, acceptance thresholds, CI/shadow deployment checks, rollback behavior, observability requirements.
- Out of scope: model retraining or developing new quant kernels (that work belongs to runtime infra).

Recommended profiles (initial draft):
- Small models (<1B params): INT8 symmetric per-channel weight + activation quantization, default clip range policy: percentile(99.9).
- Medium models (1B-7B): INT8 by default when calibration passes; otherwise FP8-e4m3 fallback. For decoder-only medium models with large context, prefer FP8 when activation dynamic range > threshold.
- Large models (>7B): FP8 (e4m3 or e5m2 depending on kernel support) as the catalog default; INT8 only for latency-critical lower-precision hardware with explicit validation.
- Mixed-precision profiles: allow layer-wise FP8/INT8 mixes for transformer blocks where per-layer calibration suggests divergent dynamic ranges.

Calibration workflow (deterministic steps):
1) Data selection: 10k representative in-domain samples per model (min 2k across different distributions). Store dataset fingerprint and provenance link.
2) Preprocess: standard tokenization, fixed random seed for sampling, run length histogram capture.
3) Per-layer statistics collection: activation histograms, per-channel min/max, second-order moments.
4) Candidate quant profile generation: auto-suggest FP8 vs INT8 per layer using heuristics (range ratio, outlier rate, KL divergence).
5) Shadow inference: run quantized model in shadow against the calibration set, capture generation metrics (perplexity, BLEU/ROUGE where applicable), token-level error histograms and latency/memory.
6) Acceptance evaluation: compare to float32 baseline using the acceptance criteria below.
7) Canary rollout: 1% traffic shadow -> 5% live A/B with automatic rollback triggers.
8) Full rollout and monitoring.

Acceptance criteria (numeric):
- Quality: relative metric delta <= 2% for generation tasks (perplexity increase <= 2% relative) OR absolute metric point thresholds for task-specific evals (e.g., ROUGE-L decrease <= 1.5 points). For instruction-following/chat flows use LLM quality score (crowd or synthetic eval) delta <= 2.5%.
- Failure modes: token corruption or hallucination spike rate <= 0.05% of tokens.
- Latency/Cost: token generation latency must improve by >= 10% or peak GPU memory reduce by >= 15% vs float baseline for the chosen profile; otherwise profile not worth defaulting.
- Reproducibility: calibration run must produce identical profile artifact (hash) across two independent runs on the same dataset and seed.

CI and gating:
- All catalog default changes create a PR with: calibration artifacts, dataset fingerprint, shadow run metrics, and auto-generated acceptance report.
- Merge gating: pass unit tests + quant-acceptance job. The CI quant-acceptance job runs a subset (~1k samples) and verifies acceptance criteria within a tolerance band.
- Canary automation: rollout automation should revert to the nearest safe fallback (FP8->INT8->float) if live drift or error rates exceed thresholds for 30m.

Guardrails and safety lattice:
- Profile allowlist per model family (e.g., code models disallow aggressive INT8 presets unless explicitly validated).
- Minimum confidence band: require two independent calibration datasets (holdout) showing similar deltas.
- Shadow staleness check: if baseline model weights or tokenizer changed since calibration, mark calibration stale and require re-run.

Observability and alerts:
- Dashboard tiles: live quality delta, token error rate, tail latency (p50/p95/p99), GPU memory usage, and model-fingerprint drift.
- Alerts: quality delta > acceptance_threshold + 0.5% fires P1 page for 15m sustained; token-error spike > threshold fires P0 immediate rollback.

Rollout playbook:
- Stage 0: QA/engineer-run calibration and review (manual sign-off).
- Stage 1: CI gated merge (artifact stored in catalog).
- Stage 2: Canary (1%->5%) with automated rollback window.
- Stage 3: Full rollout and 48h watch window with stricter alert thresholds.

Artifacts and references:
- Confluence draft: https://confluence.redwood.ai/display/INF/Quant+Playbook (placeholder).
- GitHub PR template: https://github.com/redwood-inference/model-catalog/pulls (see quant-profile-template.md).
- Calibration harness repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/quant-calib-harness (CI jobs defined).

Open questions / trade-offs:
- Threshold tuning: initial numeric thresholds are conservative; we must iterate based on 10 early-model calibrations.
- Dataset size: balance sampling cost vs coverage; we propose 10k samples as starting point but may adapt per workload.
- Metric selection for chat-wide quality is still fuzzy; we need a small user study for instruction-following models.

Next steps / immediate actions:
- (Aisha) Draft PR template + CI job (owner: Aisha) — ETA 2026-03-12.
- (Mei) Run calibration on 5 representative models (one per size bucket) and attach artifacts — ETA 2026-03-14.
- (Tomás) Add dashboard mockups and alert rules to the console board — ETA 2026-03-18.

Acceptance for this ticket: non-normative playbook merged into model-catalog repo, one end-to-end calibration artifact for each size bucket attached to the PR, CI job passing on sample datasets, and a documented rollback chain.
